title: As the Serpent Raised by Moses
description: As the Serpent Raised by Moses in Tonic Solfa to RUSTINGTON, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: John Newton wrote these words. They were printed in Olney Hymns (London, 1779), Book I, hymn 61, “Look unto me, and be ye saved. Isa 45:22”.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Eights and Sevens Double (8.7.8.7.8.7.8.7), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to RUSTINGTON; any other Eights and Sevens Double tune fits them as well.
underlay: As the ser-pent raised by Mo-ses Healed the burn-ing ser-pent's bite; Je-sus thus him-self dis-clo-ses To the woun-ded sin-ner's sight: Hear his gra-cious in-vi-ta-tion, "I have life and peace to give, I have wrought out full sal-va-tion, Sin-ner, look to me and live.

lines: As the serpent raised by Moses
Healed the burning serpent's bite;
Jesus thus himself discloses
To the wounded sinner's sight:
Hear his gracious invitation,
"I have life and peace to give,
I have wrought out full salvation,
Sinner, look to me and live.
Pore upon your sins no longer,
Well I know their mighty guilt;
But my love than death is stronger,
I my blood have freely spilt:
Though your heart has long been hardened,
Look on me--it soft shall grow;
Past transgressions shall be pardoned,
And I'll wash you white as snow.
I have seen what you were doing,
Though you little thought of me;
You were madly bent on ruin,
But I said--It shall not be:
You had been for ever wretched,
Had I not espoused your part;
Now behold my arms outstretched
To receive you to my heart.
Well may shame, and joy, and wonder,
All your inward passions move;
I could crush thee with my thunder,
But I speak to thee in love:
See! your sins are all forgiven,
I have paid the countless sum!
Now my death has opened heaven,
Thither you shall shortly come."
Dearest Savior, we adore thee
For thy precious life and death;
Melt each stubborn heart before thee,
Give us all the eye of faith:
From the law's condemning sentence,
To thy mercy we appeal;
Thou alone canst give repentance,
Thou alone our souls canst heal.

source: John Newton and William Cowper, Olney Hymns (1779)
licence: Public domain: John Newton died in 1807.
credits: Words by John Newton (1725–1807), public domain, as printed in Olney Hymns (1779); set to RUSTINGTON by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
